record.title: Radxa ZERO 3W — RK3566 quad-A55 SBC, 40-pin header, 22-pin MIPI CSI, USB-C ×2, Wi-Fi 6 / BT 5.4 (the Microduck's compute board)
record.why: electrical identity and the header/bus map are vendor-cited in iterations/v0.0.1/electrical.host.json (that record's own verdict is PASS). MECHANICAL SIDE CLOSED 2026-09-02: cad/interfaces.json now carries a measured mount-hole frame (4 x Ø2.8140, pitch 57.8429 x 22.8662, edge inset 3.5727 mm, 1 sigma 0.0396 mm) and a measured 40-pin header frame, read off Radxa's §4 raster by tools/measure_radxa_drawing.py with four negative controls PASS; the 'two disagreeing drill patterns' turned out to disagree by 0.157 mm, which an M2.5 screw absorbs, and part.py's RADXA_LONG_SPAN = 54.7 was found to be a misread and corrected to 57.8429. WHAT STILL HOLDS THE VERDICT DOWN: (1) the SKU Pollen fits is still unknown — the store's '1 GB + 32 GB' has no row in Radxa's SKU table, narrowed to two options, and one `lsblk` on a production robot settles it; (2) PCB thickness, corner radius, board mass and which corner is pin 1 are in no Radxa document at all — a calipered board and a scale settle them.
record.origin_why: electrical facts read off Radxa's own product brief (RAD-DOC-0084 rev 1.10), schematics v1.11 and v1.12, and two radxa.com pages, all fetched 2026-09-02 (iterations/v0.0.1/PROVENANCE.json); lifecycle 'active' on the brief's own sentence 'availability … until a minimum date of September 2030' (§8 p.8)
